actions.name: 双脚上升—单脚缓降提踵
actions.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: one independent PNG rehabilitation exercise photograph. The three supplied photographs are STRICT identity, wardrobe, lighting and backdrop references for the SAME woman. Preserve her exact East Asian face, apparent age, skin tone, black low ponytail, white plain short sleeve fitted athletic T-shirt, dark charcoal full length athletic pants, soft photographic light, realistic skin and cloth textures. Preserve the exact soft pale cool gray-blue subtly mottled photography backdrop color and extend it seamlessly onto the studio floor. This is a real studio photograph, not an illustration. NORMAL natural adult body proportions, approximately seven to eight heads tall, natural lengths of thighs, calves, torso, hands and feet; realistic five-finger hands and five-toed bare feet. Full body including head and both complete feet, enough margins around everything. Portrait canvas 1122 x 1402, same 4:5 proportions as references. One single continuous camera photograph with ONE woman only, no inset, no collage, no repeated figures, no written labels, no arrows, no text, no graphic overlay, no watermarks. Match references closely; only adapt pose and add the necessary simple exercise support. Barefoot so ankle and forefoot contacts are visible.
Exercise 114: eccentric heel lowering after rising on both feet. Show the single-leg lowering mid-stage, late in the controlled descent. The woman is standing upright in a right-facing near-side profile, spine and head naturally aligned, on perfectly level floor. ONE supporting leg almost straight with its whole ball of foot and toes grounded; that supporting heel is only 1–2 cm off the flat floor, visibly a very low heel raise. Her other knee bends gently so the non-training foot is clearly suspended a small distance behind the supporting calf; it has no ground contact. ONE hand LIGHTLY touches a fixed matte gray waist-height handrail with solid stable base. The other arm hangs relaxed. No dumbbell, no external weight. Do not make an exaggerated tiptoe at the top. No step, no platform, no incline board, no jumping. Natural arm, leg and foot anatomy. Side view allows the low supporting heel, forefoot contact, and separate lifted foot to be unambiguously visible. Keep entire rail and subject sensibly composed without occluding her face or feet.

corrections.reason: 首图支撑跟过高，接近顶部。
corrections.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET; images 2, 3, 4 are the original identity, outfit, lighting and gray-blue backdrop references. Make ONE local pose correction to the supporting bare foot and ankle in image 1: it is too high on tiptoe. Lower the supporting heel toward the same flat floor so the heel is JUST 1–2 cm above the floor, a very narrow visible gap; the supporting foot is almost flat, with only a slight 5–10 degree upward heel tilt. Keep the supporting ball of foot and toes in their EXACT original grounded place. This is the late stage of controlled single-leg eccentric heel lowering, not the high top of a calf raise. Relax and reduce plantarflexion to lower heel; the foot must stay normal anatomy, full-length heel to toes. Lower the rest of the body only a tiny matching amount if biomechanically necessary. Preserve the woman's exact face, age, ponytail, white T-shirt, dark charcoal pants, proportions, entire upper body, hand lightly on gray handrail, other hand relaxed, NON-SUPPORTING knee bent with that foot OFF the floor in the same position. Preserve photographic lighting, framing, pale gray-blue mottled studio background and floor EXACTLY. Output one PNG portrait 1122x1402 with full person and feet, no text, no arrows, no diagram, no collage. No dumbbell, no steps. Avoid redesigning the scene. Only lower the supporting heel to near-floor.

corrections.reason: 进一步降低支撑跟，呈现接近平地的缓降阶段。
corrections.prompt: EDIT TARGET image 1; images 2–4 lock the original woman's exact face, hairstyle, clothes, colors and photographic background. Lower the single supporting heel MUCH MORE. In image 1 the supporting heel is STILL too high. The finished supporting FOOT SHOULD LOOK ALMOST FLAT on the ground: supporting toe/ball contact at the existing floor position; supporting HEEL SOLE at essentially the same horizontal level as toe contact, but a tiny visible 1 cm gap remains beneath heel. Its long sole line is nearly horizontal, only 5–8 degrees tilted, NOT 30 degrees. The heel sole should be about 8–12 image pixels above the floor at this framing. It should resemble a foot about to finish landing heel down, not standing on tiptoe. Reduce ankle plantarflexion; lower the body a tiny matching amount naturally if needed while staying upright. Keep the opposite knee flexed and foot clearly airborne behind, hand lightly on fixed gray waist-high rail, relaxed other hand. Preserve normal anatomy, identity, proportions and entire photograph composition. Do not change background, wardrobe or rail. One continuous full body studio photograph. Portrait PNG 1122x1402. No words, arrows, overlay or collage.
